Execute with remaining arguments --- Skill Name: hallmark Path: /Users/amin/dev/p-projects/armenia/kuchup/.cursor/skills/hallmark/SKILL.md SKILL.md content: # Hallmark A design skill for AI coding assistants. Makes the UIs they generate look made, not generated. Hallmark is opinionated, short, and boring on purpose. It encodes a tight set of rules — drawn from the consensus of the anti-AI-slop design field (Anthropic's frontend-design skill, the Claude cookbook on frontend aesthetics, and the 2026 "tactile rebellion" movement) — and refuses to let the model fall back to the defaults every LLM was trained on. The differentiator: Hallmark insists on **structural variety**, not just visual variety. Two pages by Hallmark for two different briefs should not share the same hero → 3-feature → CTA → footer rhythm. They should feel like different sites, not different colour-swaps of the same template. See [`references/structure.md`](references/structure.md). **Powered by Together AI.** --- ## How to use this skill Hallmark has one default behaviour and three explicit verbs. | Invocation | What it does | | --- | --- | | *(default)* | The user asked you to design or build something new. Follow the **Design flow** below. | | `hallmark audit ` | Read the target, score it against the anti-pattern list, return a ranked punch list. **Do not edit.** | | `hallmark redesign [--mood ]` | Take the target's content and intent, then redesign the visual structure **inside the existing implementation boundaries unless the user explicitly confirms a full rebuild.** New section rhythm, new heading placement, new component voice. Preserve existing routes, component ownership, copy intent, brand, and information architecture; replace only the visual/interaction layer needed for the requested scope. | | `hallmark study ` | The user pasted or attached an image of a design they admire, **or** pasted a URL to a live page. Extract the **DNA** — macrostructure, archetypes, type-pairing, colour anchor — and produce a diagnosis report, then optionally rebuild the user's content using the extracted DNA **or** emit a portable `design.md` of the DNA. Detection is automatic: a URL (`http://` / `https://` prefix) routes to URL mode; anything else routes to image mode. **URL mode** reads the page's HTML and CSS via WebFetch — it can name exact fonts and exact colour values, but can't judge rhythm. After the diagnosis, the user has three follow-ups: build with the DNA (handoff to default), lock the DNA into a portable `design.md` (opt-in via "lock the DNA" / "give me a design.md"), or stop at the diagnosis. **Never copies pixels. Refuses template-marketplace URLs. Tighter refusal layer for `design.md` emission than for the diagnosis itself — URL-mode emission requires attestation that the source is the user's own or a public reference for their own brand. Falls back to asking for a screenshot if the URL is auth-walled, a JS-only SPA shell, or otherwise un-readable.** Load [`references/study.md`](references/study.md) before this verb runs. | If the user types anything that does not clearly map to `audit`, `redesign`, or `study`, treat it as default. If the user attaches an image or pastes a URL without a verb prefix, ask: *"Should I `study` this (extract the DNA), or should I treat it as a reference for a fresh build?"* **Implementation safety rail.** Hallmark is a design skill, not a license to bulldoze a codebase. In any existing project: - Never delete production files, route trees, component directories, or an old website unless the user explicitly asks for deletion or approves a file-level plan that lists the deletions. - Default to in-place edits of the named files, or additive new components/tokens that are wired through the existing route. If the redesign would require removing multiple components, stop and ask for confirmation first. - Treat PDFs, README files, `.md` briefs, docs, transcripts, and pitch decks as reference material. Do **not** copy them word-for-word into the page unless the user explicitly says to use that text verbatim. - Before editing, state the exact files you expect to modify/create/delete. Deletions require explicit confirmation. The default Design flow always picks a theme. By default it picks one of the **20 named themes** — the *catalog* — and rotates among them per the diversification rule. There is also a quiet *custom* branch that constructs a one-off OKLCH palette + free-font pairing for the brief; the custom route fires **only when the brief carries a creative-intent signal** (the user names a brand colour, names a multi-attribute vibe the catalog can't carry, or explicitly asks for a custom theme). For vanilla briefs, the user never sees the words "catalog" or "custom" — the catalog runs silently. See Step 1 (signal detection) and Step 2.6 (dispatch); the protocol lives in [`references/custom-theme.md`](references/custom-theme.md). --- ## Disciplines that hold across every verb These six disciplines are **not** verb-specific. They apply to default Design, `audit`, `redesign`, `study`, and component-scope alike. They sit alongside the slop test, not inside one branch of it. 1. **Pre-emit self-critique.** Before handing back any output, score it 1–5 on six axes — Philosophy, Hierarchy, Execution, Specificity, Restraint, Variety. Anything **< 3** triggers a revision pass. Stamp the six scores at the top of the artifact (`/* Hallmark · pre-emit critique: P5 H4 E5 S4 R5 V5 */`). See [`references/slop-test.md`](references/slop-test.md) § Pre-emit self-critique. 2. **Honest copy — no fabricated content.** If the user did not supply a metric, do not invent one. Stat-led layouts, comparison rows, and proof bars must use real numbers, a placeholder (`—` plus a labelled grey block, "metric to confirm"), or a different macrostructure. *"+47 % conversion"*, *"trusted by 50,000+ teams"*, and *"10× faster"* are slop the moment they're invented. Same rule for testimonials, logos, and case-study counts. See [`references/anti-patterns.md` § Invented metrics](references/anti-patterns.md) and slop-test gate **46**. 3. **Locked tokens — no mid-render improvisation.** Once a theme is selected at Step 2.6, every colour and every `font-family` declaration in the artifact must reference a named token (`var(--color-accent)`, `font-family: var(--font-display)`). Inline OKLCH / hex / `rgb()` values, or a `font-family: "Some Font"` declaration that bypasses the token block, are not allowed. If a value is needed that doesn't exist as a token, lift it into the token block as a new named variable, then reference it. See [`references/anti-patterns.md` § Mid-render token improvisation](references/anti-patterns.md) and slop-test gate **48**. 4. **Re-drawn chrome forbidden.** Hallmark must not hand-build fake browser bars (URL pill + traffic-light dots), fake phone frames, fake code-block windows (mock title bar + dots wrapping a `
`), or fake IDE chrome — the user's environment already supplies real chrome. Use real screenshots wrapped in a `

input.plan:
# Company workspace redesign (LinkedIn first impression)

Going with: **audience** = senior candidates arriving from LinkedIn · **use** = feel this is a high-end application studio, then apply · **tone** = luxury / restrained. If any of those is wrong, say so before implementation.

`design.md` is already the locked system. This is a **single-page, in-place restyle** of the company workspace. No rebuild, no shadcn, no new theme, no board/homepage work.

## Pre-flight (preserved)

- **Fonts:** Lexend + Manrope + JetBrains Mono (`company.html` Google Fonts + [`relocation_jobs/static/design-tokens.css`](relocation_jobs/static/design-tokens.css))
- **Palette:** Warm Horizon (ivory paper, navy ink, orange accent ≤ 5%)
- **Motion:** CSS only; existing `--ease-out` / `--dur-short`; no Framer/GSAP
- **Framework:** vanilla HTML/CSS/JS (not the React board in `frontend/`)
- **Stamp today:** Workbench + `designed-as-app` at the top of [`relocation_jobs/static/styles.css`](relocation_jobs/static/styles.css)

Hallmark will preserve: tokens, fonts, CTA voice, status-layer hues, `<position-card>` APIs.
Hallmark will introduce: Split Studio rhythm, luxury density, progressive disclosure, candidate-facing empty copy.

ui-ux-pro-max’s `--design-system` rec (dark zinc + Cormorant) is **rejected** — it fights brand and `design.md`. Keep Swiss/minimal spacing, density 3, motion 2.

## What this page is

Route: `/company/<country>/<slug>` → [`relocation_jobs/static/company.html`](relocation_jobs/static/company.html) + [`relocation_jobs/static/js/company.js`](relocation_jobs/static/js/company.js). Status/ATS/pin live in shared [`relocation_jobs/static/js/position-card.js`](relocation_jobs/static/js/position-card.js) (also used on the board). Company CSS is the block from ~L6650 in [`styles.css`](relocation_jobs/static/styles.css).

The current first impression fails luxury because everything is equally loud: duplicate titles, a full rainbow of status pills (desktop `.position-actions-secondary` is always a 4-col grid), MCP-jargon empty states, equal-weight LaTeX + PDF panes.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph today [Today]
    H1[Header plus company H1]
    Rail[Positions rail]
    Dup[Card repeats title]
    Status[All status pills]
    Split[Equal LaTeX and PDF]
  end
  subgraph next [Split Studio]
    Mast[Quiet masthead]
    QuietRail[Quiet role list]
    Stage[Role once plus Apply]
    Proof[PDF as proof]
    Work[LaTeX as working half]
  end
  today --> next
```

## Structural fingerprint

- **Genre:** modern-minimal (locked)
- **Macrostructure:** Split Studio — diptych: roles | studio, then working copy | PDF proof
- **Nav:** keep existing company header; restyle toward quiet edge-aligned chrome (wordmark + breadcrumb left, Application data / Sign out as text-style). No new nav component.
- **Footer:** none (app page)
- **Enrichment:** none — function carries the page
- **Motion:** CTA press already in tokens; hover lift on Apply only; reduced-motion already in `styles.css`

Amend [`design.md`](design.md) first (Hallmark rule: don’t locally override the system):

- App family stays Workbench for the board
- **Company workspace MAY use Split Studio**, spacious density, secondary actions behind More, PDF as the proof half

## Layout (keep IA, change rhythm)

1. **Masthead** — Compact lockup, `Job panel / GERMANY`, company name as the one display line. Drop the redundant “Application workspace” subtitle. Header buttons stay; they stop competing with Apply.
2. **Roles rail** — Same list and selection. Selected item: hairline + small accent mark, not a loud orange card. Badges use status tokens (replace hardcoded `#0d9488` / `#2563eb` in `.company-position-badge--*`).
3. **Stage** — Role title once. Hide the card’s duplicate `.position-title-row` (and CV-ready badges) under `.company-layout` only. Primary: **Apply on company site** (orange). Secondary as text/quiet pills: Show description, Re-render, Download. Posting URL stays, as a single muted link, not a dumped raw URL paragraph.
4. **Status** — All actions remain. On this page only, collapse `.position-actions-secondary` behind the existing More control (desktop already shows them always — that is the rainbow row in the screenshot). Status chips stay on the design.md status layer, chip-scale.
5. **Studio** — CV | Cover tab rail stays (already one-line scroll). **PDF is the larger proof column** (`1.15fr` / `0.85fr` on desktop). LaTeX starts inside a native `<details>` (“Source”) so seniors see the document first; Edit/Save stay inside it.
6. **Empty states** — Candidate-facing, three beats (Hallmark copy): name what’s missing, why it matters, one next step. Keep the MCP/Connect link, demote it.

Example empty copy (not MCP-first):

- “No CV for this role yet.”
- “Mark Looking to apply, then generate a tailored CV from Cursor or Claude.”
- Link: How MCP works

## Files (modify / create / delete)

**Modify**

- [`design.md`](design.md) — per-page Split Studio allowance
- [`relocation_jobs/static/company.html`](relocation_jobs/static/company.html) — header/workspace classes, LaTeX `<details>`, empty copy, bump `styles.css?v=` / `company.js?v=`
- [`relocation_jobs/static/styles.css`](relocation_jobs/static/styles.css) — rewrite the company-layout block (~L6650–7063) + scoped `.company-layout position-card` overrides; stamp the company block, do not replace the global Workbench stamp
- [`relocation_jobs/static/js/company.js`](relocation_jobs/static/js/company.js) — `emptyTexMessage` / `emptyPdfMessage` / detail-empty copy only

**Create**

- [`.hallmark/log.json`](.hallmark/log.json) — one `designed-as-app` entry (`macrostructure: Split Studio`, `theme: Warm Horizon`)

**Do not delete** any routes, `position-card.js`, board CSS, or homepage files.

**Do not touch** `position-card.js` behaviour (shared with the board). Company-only look is CSS under `.company-layout`.

**Do not add** shadcn, Tailwind, new fonts, dark mode, or a parallel `design-system/MASTER.md`.

## Ponytail constraints

- CSS-first. Native `<details>` for Source. No new JS framework, no new HTTP file.
- Reuse `--control-*`, `.header-primary-btn`, `.tab-rail`, status tokens.
- Named spacing tokens (`var(--space-md)` etc.), no new hex in company CSS.
- Skip extracting `company.css` (extra request for no gain).

## Verification

- Browser on local panel (`PANEL_SCRAPE_ENABLED=1`, :5051): open a company with a position, switch roles, CV/cover tabs, JD toggle, More status actions, Apply, empty vs PDF-ready states.
- Check 375 / 768 / desktop. No two-line button labels. Tab rail scrolls, does not wrap.
- Confirm the **board** still shows the full status row (company overrides must not leak).

## Hallmark preview (what we will ship)

- **Macrostructure** · Split Studio (company workspace allowance in `design.md`)
- **Theme** · Warm Horizon (ivory paper · navy ink · orange accent · Lexend / Manrope)
- **Enrichment** · none
- **Sections** · Masthead · Roles rail · Role stage · Status (collapsed) · Studio (PDF proof + Source)
- **Motion** · Apply press · More expand · reduced-motion opacity
- **Slop test** · run after Build (locked tokens, no italic headers, no invented metrics, no fake chrome)

*System already locked in `design.md`. Implementation amends that file, then restyles this page.*
